text:
mike: FYI ran the nightly eval against the canary with the new scheduler-kernel-swap heuristic and we're seeing a quality regression on the JSON-output eval set (structured outputs get partially truncated / malformed).

anya: ugh, details? EM/ROUGE/whatever numbers?

mike: EM down ~3.7% (baseline -> 0.937 -> 0.900), hallucination rate up (more stray keys). Repro steps below. Also observed a latency spike during kernel handoff in perf traces.

sophia: can you paste the perf snippet and the broken output example?

mike: perf snippet:
```
kernel_switch_latency_ms: mean=18.3 p95=22.1 p99=120.4
kv_cache_miss_rate: baseline=2.1% -> canary=14.3%
batcher_block_time_ms: tail spikes coincident with swap
callsite: scheduler->kernel_manager::swap_if_needed()
```
Broken JSON from eval-run (truncated / invalid):
```
{"request_id": "abcd-1234", "answer": "{\"choices\": [{\"text\": \"The winner is...\"}], \"meta\": {\"score\": 0.92}}"
```
(you can see nesting got mangled, missing escape/closing)

mike: repro run that hits it reliably:
```
export RUN_MODE=calib-chain
./perf_eval --model mix-fp8-int4 --prompt-set json-eval --batch 1 --seed 42 --kv-length 1024
```
Run on pool `dedicated-gpu-pool-3` reproduces ~1/10 runs; higher kv-length increases probability.

anya: hypothesis: calibration step triggers a kernel variant swap while requests still hold references to old KV layout -> partial flush or index mismatch. That could yield malformed structured output when streaming writer expects kv keys that were reclaimed.

lee: there was a tiny change yesterday in the scheduler that opportunistically switches kernel iff predicted latency benefit > 5ms. I can roll that back on canary.

sophia: also saw telemetry showing an uptick of `kv_index_rebind` events right at the time of the swap. I'll attach the trace links.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: deploy 2024-11-05T13:22:01 by lee to canary (rev: ab12cd3).

mike: thanks @lee. For triage: we should decide whether this is a functional correctness bug (KV layout invariants broken) or a timing regression that just exposes a race in the output serializer. If functional, block rollout; if timing, we can add a gate to prevent swaps mid-request.

anya: quick mitigation options:
- pin kernel variant for requests that indicate long KV chains (flag at router)
- add lightweight quiesce: wait for in-flight kv refs to drain before swap (cheap but adds latency)
- fallback: if malformed structured output is detected at serializer, re-run generation with pinned kernel (costly)

sophia: I can add a quick check in serializer to validate JSON structure and emit a metric + requeue for the failing case. That will reduce user impact while we fix root cause.

lee: I'll revert the opportunistic switch on canary immediately and re-run the eval. If that clears, we know scheduler change is responsible.

mike: request: @anya can you grab full perf traces (CPU + GPU timings) and the kernel selection logs around the swap? I think the kernel manager prints `swap_decision={old:...,new:...,reason:...}` if enabled.

anya: on it. Linking traces when ready: https://telemetry.redwood/trace/abcd-quant-swap-220123

mike: thanks. Also, watch out for calibration table updates: some models perform per-batch re-calibration which can mutate quant tables mid-flight. If the quant table id changes, kernel codepaths may assume a different scaling which could cause token misalignment in structured output.

sophia: noted. I'll instrument `calib.table_id` and `kv.cache_epoch` so we can correlate table mutations with kv index churn.

lee: rolling back now, will ping when canary has new build.

deploy-bot: canary rollback triggered by lee -> rev ab12cd3 reverted to rev 9f8e7d6.

mike: after rollback, quick smoke shows JSON-output EM back to baseline on a small sample. Good signal but need full run.

anya: collecting full run logs + traces, ETA ~25m. Will paste compressed link.

mike: next steps (agreed):
1) leave rollback on canary until PR with fix lands
2) sophia to add serializer guard + metric for malformed structured outputs
3) anya to gather and attach traces + selection logs and correlate with calib table id changes
4) lee to add a safety gate in scheduler to avoid swaps while kv refs > 0 (or to only swap at safe breakpoints)

sophia: adding a ticket for serializer guard and alert: INF-1234.

mike: thanks team :thumbsup: let's keep updates brief here.

lee: update: full eval job after rollback finished, EM delta went back within noise (+0.2%). I'll open a PR to make the swap conditional on `inflight_kv_refs == 0 || kv_age > 1s`.

anya: logs + traces uploaded: https://s3.redwood/triage/2201234567-traces.tar.gz (contains kernel logs, perf profiles, calib table snapshots)

mike: perfect. We'll re-run the canary with the fix in a controlled window. If anyone sees repro locally, drop the small trace id here so we can correlate.

sophia: will do.
